study: Kitmitto et al. 2018 — EEF Thinking, Doing, Talking Science (effectiveness trial); AIR evaluation
eval_evidence: EEF effectiveness trial independently evaluated by the American Institutes for Research (AIR); registered ISRCTN22499525. Developers (the 'Oxford team') ran the programme but did not conduct the impact evaluation.
developer_evidence: Key adaptation of this effectiveness trial: the developers did NOT deliver CPD to teachers. TDTS 'was delivered to 233 Year 5 teachers through 4 CPD days... led by pairs of experts who were trained in the TDTS model by the programme developers' — i.e., trained intermediary trainers delivered, not the developers themselves.
cascade_evidence: Explicit train-the-trainer model (developer -> trainer -> teacher). The Oxford team (developers) trained pairs of expert trainers, who then delivered the CPD to school teachers — ≥1 extra transmission hop; report contrasts this with the earlier developer-delivered efficacy trial.
counterfactual_evidence: Two-arm trial with a 'business as usual' waitlist control group; control schools received no alternative science PD during the trial year.
coaching_evidence: Intervention = 4 CPD days staggered across the year (plus in-school planning time). Report states there was 'no intention that trainers would act as coaches or mentors between sessions' — no ongoing in-class coaching.
student_dose_evidence: Teacher-facing CPD only (two teachers per school attended); changes the teacher's Year 5 science instruction. No tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Effectiveness trial run in a single year (2016-17) with trainers delivering for the first time and teachers new to TDTS; outcomes measured at end of that first implementation year (June 2017).
